subject: Urgent: Your Account Will Be Suspended
body:
Dear Customer,

We've detected unusual activity on your account. Your PayPal account will be suspended within 24 hours unless you verify your information immediately.

Click here to secure your account: http://paypal-verification.secure-site.net/login

PayPal Security Team
explanation: This is a phishing attempt. Red flags: suspicious domain (paypal-alert.com instead of paypal.com), urgency tactics, and the verification link goes to a non-PayPal domain.

subject: Your Monthly Statement is Ready
body:
Dear Valued Customer,

Your monthly statement for January 2024 is now available in your online banking portal.

To view your statement, please log in to your account at chase.com using your regular credentials.

Thank you for banking with us.
explanation: This is legitimate. The email comes from the official Chase domain, doesn't ask for credentials directly, and directs users to the official website without suspicious links.

subject: RE: Invoice #INV-2024-0198
body:
Hi,

Please find the updated invoice attached. There was an error in the previous calculation.

Best regards,
Maria Rodriguez
Accounts Department
explanation: This is likely phishing. It's an unexpected invoice with an urgent tone, comes from an unknown sender, and has a suspicious attachment that could contain malware.

subject: Password Reset Confirmation
body:
Hello,

We received a request to reset the password for your Microsoft account. If you requested this change, no further action is needed.

If you didn't request this password reset, please secure your account immediately by visiting account.microsoft.com.

Microsoft Account Team
explanation: This is legitimate. It comes from the official Microsoft domain, provides helpful information without forcing action, and directs to the official Microsoft website.

subject: Congratulations! You've Won $50,000!
body:
CONGRATULATIONS!

You have been selected as a winner in our International Email Lottery! You've won $50,000 USD!

To claim your prize, please send your full name, address, and bank details to: claims@lottery-winner.net

Claim within 48 hours or forfeit your winnings!
explanation: Classic phishing scam. Red flags: too good to be true prize, requests personal/financial information, urgency pressure, and suspicious sender domain.

subject: Meeting Tomorrow - Q1 Planning Session
body:
Hi Team,

Just a reminder about our Q1 planning meeting tomorrow at 2 PM in Conference Room B. Please bring your project proposals.

Agenda:
- Budget review
- Project priorities
- Resource allocation

Thanks,
Sarah
explanation: This is legitimate internal communication. It comes from your company domain, contains specific business details, and matches normal workplace communication patterns.

subject: FINAL NOTICE: IRS Tax Settlement
body:
FINAL NOTICE

This is your FINAL NOTICE regarding unpaid taxes of $3,247.83. Immediate action required to avoid legal consequences.

Call 1-800-TAX-SCAM immediately to speak with an agent and arrange payment.

FAILURE TO RESPOND WILL RESULT IN ARREST WARRANT.
explanation: This is a phishing scam impersonating the IRS. Red flags: IRS doesn't email about taxes, threatening language, fake domain (gov-tax.org), and pressure tactics.

subject: Your Order #ORD789123 Has Shipped
body:
Hello,

Great news! Your order has shipped and is on its way.

Order #ORD789123
Estimated delivery: January 16, 2024

Track your package: amazon.com/orders

Thank you for shopping with Amazon!
explanation: This appears legitimate. It comes from the official Amazon domain, contains specific order details, and directs to the official Amazon website for tracking.

subject: Urgent: Update Your Banking Information
body:
Dear Customer,

Due to new security regulations, you must update your banking information within 24 hours.

Click here to update: https://fnb-secure-update.verification-site.com/update-info

Your account will be frozen if you don't comply.

First National Bank
explanation: This is phishing. Red flags: suspicious sender domain with extra subdomains, urgency tactics, threatening account freeze, and the update link goes to a non-bank domain.

subject: Team Building Event - Save the Date
body:
Dear Team,

We're excited to announce our annual team building event on February 15th at Riverside Park.

Activities include:
- Team challenges
- BBQ lunch
- Awards ceremony

More details to follow. Please mark your calendars!

Best regards,
HR Team
explanation: This is legitimate internal communication. It comes from your company's HR department, contains realistic event details, and matches typical corporate communication style.
